headline: 英倫藝文三則速報
context: 衛報本輪評論同樣橫跨舞台、音樂與書籍。愛丁堡藝穗節作品《Goodbye Dandelion》講述一段相差五十歲的忘年之交；波蘭傳統舞曲oberek，正被新一代音樂人混進電子樂與芝加哥腳步舞（footwork），玩出新花樣；新出版的芭芭拉・卡特蘭（Barbara Cartland）傳記，重新認真檢視這位暢銷小說家傳奇的一生。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Underbelly, Edinburgh Maddie and Marcus Rice relate with words and songs the lessons passed on from one woman to a younger one An unexpected theme on this year’s Edinburgh fringe is assisted dying. It is central to Morna Young’s After Party , about a matriarch who chooses to die after her 80th birthday, and Ben Harrison’s adaptation of Andrew O’Hagan’s Mayflies , in which a terminally ill man travels to Dignitas. It is hinted at in Eilidh Loan’s Cathy , about a woman adjusting to bereavement. And it is here again in this breezy storytelling show by sibling duo Maddie and Marcus Rice. The semi-fictional tale is about Maddie’s befriending of the 87-year-old Darcy O’Shea, an artist and piano teacher 50 years her senior, who is full of zest and vigour. As Maddie puts it, she is “unapologetically herself”, a woman living a life of happy self-reliance with limited tolerance for anyone else. A long-gone partner nicknamed her Dandelion because of her sticky-up hair, and it suits her personality. At Underbelly, Edinburgh, until 30 August All our Edinburgh reviews Continue reading...
sources.title: Goodbye Dandelion review – ode to a fabulous friendship with a 50-year age gap

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: The oberek is a traditional dance beloved of state folk ensembles – but a new generation of musicians is reconfiguring its music into wild new forms, merging folk steps with electronics and the sound of Chicago footwork It’s 6pm on the first day of OFF festival in Katowice, and a crowd is gathering in front of one of the stages to watch newcomers Tercet Imperial. Sporting disco outfits of nylon jackets, tracksuits and Chicago Bulls caps, keyboardist Piotr Zabrodzki deploys resonant acid melodies, while drummer Jan Emil Młynarski plays a rapid, irregular rhythm that brings to mind the scattergun beats of footwork, the ghetto-house subgenre that grew out of Chicago in the late 90s. Not many of those jerking their limbs to the music in front of the stage are likely to realise that they are listening to a distinctly Polish sound: that of the oberek, a traditional dance in triple metre whose name derives from the Polish verb “to spin”, because it usually accompanies couples whirling across dancefloors in a circular motion. sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: A brilliant new biography that does it subject the favour of taking her seriously – even if few else did Barbara Cartland was famous for dictating her novels. With a pekingese clamped to her hot pink bosom she would lie back on a library couch and exhale a story about virginal girls taming wayward dukes, damaged airmen or misunderstood surgeons. Meanwhile Miss Savory, Mrs Smith or Mrs Morgan, picked for being unfidgety and sneezeless, would take everything down in immaculate Pitman shorthand. Cartland reckoned on being able to polish off 8,000 words a day. “In this way,” she told one of the many reporters who quizzed her on her astonishing productivity, “the typescript for an 80,000-word novel is finished in a fortnight.” At her peak she was pushing out 23 books a year which added up to 723 in total. Only Agatha Christie and William Shakespeare topped her lifetime sales of 750m. Cartland was a dictator in other ways, too. Husbands, dogs, houses and the local council were all expected to bend themselves to her indomitable will. Resistance, let alone opposition, was futile. The managing director of the company that printed her books suggested that she read Nietzsche on the perceptive grounds that they had a lot of ideas in common. Oddly, he also declared himself madly in love with her. Behind that marshmallowy exterior, all pink chiffon, candyfloss hair and soft, smudgy lines, there lurked sinews of high-tensile steel. thread_text: 衛報本輪評論一樣橫跨舞台、音樂與書籍。愛丁堡藝穗節作品《Goodbye Dandelion》，講一段相差五十歲的忘年之交——年輕作者跟87歲、活力十足的畫家兼鋼琴老師結為好友。波蘭傳統舞曲oberek，正被新一代音樂人混進電子樂與芝加哥腳步舞（footwork），在音樂節上玩出意想不到的新花樣。新出版的芭芭拉・卡特蘭（Barbara Cartland）傳記，則認真回顧這位一生寫了723本小說、銷量僅次於莎士比亞與阿嘉莎・克莉絲蒂的傳奇作家。
threads_text: 衛報本輪評論一樣橫跨舞台、音樂與書籍。愛丁堡藝穗節今年悄悄流行起「善終」主題，這齣《Goodbye Dandelion》講的則是一段相差五十歲的忘年之交——年輕作者跟87歲、活力十足的畫家兼鋼琴老師結為好友，用故事跟歌曲，記下老人家教她的人生課。音樂這邊，波蘭傳統舞曲oberek，正被新一代音樂人混進電子樂與芝加哥腳步舞（footwork），在音樂節上玩出意想不到的新花樣。書籍這邊，新出版的芭芭拉・卡特蘭（Barbara Cartland）傳記，認真回顧這位一天能口述8000字、一生寫了723本小說、銷量僅次於莎士比亞與阿嘉莎・克莉絲蒂的傳奇作家。
voice_text: 這輪評論一樣橫跨舞台、音樂跟書。先看舞台劇。愛丁堡藝穗節有一齣《Goodbye Dandelion》，講一段相差五十歲的忘年之交——年輕作者，跟一位87歲、活力十足的畫家兼鋼琴老師，變成了好朋友。換個調性，聊音樂。波蘭有一種傳統舞曲叫oberek，現在被新一代音樂人拿去混電子樂、混芝加哥的腳步舞，在音樂節上玩出很不一樣的味道。最後看書。有一本新出版的傳記，重新認真回顧芭芭拉・卡特蘭的一生——她一輩子寫了723本小說，銷量在暢銷作家裡，僅次於莎士比亞跟阿嘉莎・克莉絲蒂。
